title: Learning Word-Level Explanations of Text Reuse in Latin Literature with Little Annotation
abstract: arXiv:2611.18319v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Detecting an intertextual reference is only the first step; philologists also need to know how a later author reworked the source. We explain a reuse pair word by word: each word of the reusing passage is first aligned to its source word, then labeled with the operation that transformed it, such as a copy, a change of inflection, or a substitution. Such word-level operations are expensive to annotate, and only a few corpora annotated at this level exist for text reuse in Latin literature. We describe a procedure that needs only a limited number of annotations: synthetic pairs, built by applying known operations to Latin text, train a first model, and active learning chooses the pairs an annotator corrects. Among several architectures, a model that links and labels together performs best: a pointer network that, for every reuse word, chooses a source word and names the operation in the same step. translated_title: 用少量标注学习拉丁文学中文本复用的词级解释
translated_abstract: 检测互文性指涉只是第一步；语文学家还需要知道后世作者是如何改写原始文献的。我们对复用文本对进行逐词解释：复用段落中的每个词首先与其源文本中的词进行对齐，然后用改变它的操作来标注，例如复制、屈折变化或替换。这类词级操作的标注成本高昂，目前针对拉丁文学文本复用、在此层级上进行标注的语料库仅有少数几个。我们提出了一种只需少量标注即可完成的方法：通过对拉丁文本应用已知操作构建合成文本对来训练第一个模型，再由主动学习挑选出需要标注者修正的文本对。在多种架构中，将链接与标注合并为一个步骤的模型表现最佳：即一个指针网络，它对复用段落中的每个词，在同一步骤中选出对应的源词并给出所执行的操作。我们证明，借助主动学习，仅需200个文本对即可……
tldr: 该论文提出一种仅需少量标注的方法：先利用合成文本对训练模型，再通过主动学习优化，最终用指针网络对拉丁文学中的文本复用进行词级对齐与改写操作标注，从而解释后世作者如何改写原文。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a low-annotation approach that trains a pointer network via synthetic pairs and active learning to jointly align and label word-level reuse operations, explaining how later Latin authors reworked their source texts.
